text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- German constitutional court demands case-by-case examination of former Stasi informers and ex-East German communist party functionaries before barring or sacking them from public service
- In June no upturn in jobs market. Unemployment has dropped slightly. Bernhard Jagoda, president of the Federal Labour Office, says jobs market has stabilised in western Germany
- Hardly any hope for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's tax reform
- Data security is a key issue for Global Information Networks. European countries issue Bonn declaration on commerce on the Internet at end of two-day conference
- German investors are optimistic after Mexican elections
HANDELSBLATT
- Ex-East Geramn communist party members can not be automatically barred from public service. German supreme court rules they must be examined on a case-by-case basis
- Unemployment drops slightly, German Federal Labour Office also notes an improvement in western Germany.
- Bonn plans to convert its old debt into the euro, Europe's planned single currency
- European countries declare that Internet will not be burdened with extra taxes and regulations
- The opposition Social Democrats speak of an agreement in a row over tax.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Number of unemployed is not going up anymore.
- Not every former East German communist party member or former secret police informer can justifiably be barred or sacked from public service.
- Tax negotiations in Bonn have broken down
- German stock exchange celebrate a record high at over 4,000 points.
- Germans earning marks live best in Czech republic
DIE WELT

- Success for former East German communist functionaries, as German Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe rules ex-party members and also people who informed for the Ministry for State Security (Stasi) can not be automatically barred from their jobs in public service and that these must be considered case-bay-case
- Unemployment figures drop slightly in June. Job market shows stable trend.
- German army says video showing German soldiers staging mock executions and rapes is fake. Experts will examine whether soldiers were really involved. Prosecutors investigate the case
- DAX jumps 4,000 point hurdle. Analysts expect further rise, saying enough liquidity is present
